Alguns relatos indicam que certos ataques ainda podem ser conduzidos diretamente pelos desenvolvedores principais do ransomware. Fontes públicas também se referem ao grupo como "Spearwing" ou "Medusa Actors". O Medusa Group emprega técnicas baseadas em recursos nativos do sistema (living off the land), utilizando com frequência ferramentas públicas e softwares comuns de gerenciamento remoto. O grupo pratica a dupla extorsão, exfiltrando dados antes da criptografia e ameaçando publicar as informações roubadas caso o resgate não seja pago…

nodes.name: BRONZE BUTLER
nodes.description: BRONZE BUTLER is a cyber espionage group with likely Chinese origins that has been active since at least 2008. The group primarily targets Japanese organizations, particularly those in government, biotechnology, electronics manufacturing, and industrial chemistry.
nodes.description_pt: BRONZE BUTLER é um grupo de ciberespionagem de provável origem chinesa, ativo desde pelo menos 2008. O grupo ataca principalmente organizações japonesas, em especial dos setores governamental, de biotecnologia, de fabricação de eletrônicos e de química industrial.

nodes.name: TA551
nodes.description: TA551 is a financially-motivated threat group that has been active since at least 2018. The group has primarily targeted English, German, Italian, and Japanese speakers through email-based malware distribution campaigns.
nodes.description_pt: TA551 é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira, ativo desde pelo menos 2018. O grupo ataca principalmente falantes de inglês, alemão, italiano e japonês por meio de campanhas de distribuição de malware por e-mail.

nodes.name: TEMP.Veles
nodes.description: TEMP.Veles is a Russia-based threat group that has targeted critical infrastructure. The group has been observed utilizing TRITON, a malware framework designed to manipulate industrial safety systems.
nodes.description_pt: TEMP.Veles é um grupo de ameaça sediado na Rússia que ataca infraestrutura crítica. O grupo foi observado utilizando o TRITON, um framework de malware projetado para manipular sistemas de segurança industrial.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.description: Equation is a sophisticated threat group that employs multiple remote access tools. The group is known to use zero-day exploits and has developed the capability to overwrite the firmware of hard disk drives.
nodes.description_pt: Equation é um grupo de ameaça sofisticado que emprega diversas ferramentas de acesso remoto. O grupo é conhecido por utilizar explorações de dia zero e desenvolveu a capacidade de sobrescrever o firmware de discos rígidos.

nodes.name: BackdoorDiplomacy
nodes.description: BackdoorDiplomacy is a cyber espionage threat group that has been active since at least 2017. BackdoorDiplomacy has targeted Ministries of Foreign Affairs and telecommunication companies in Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
nodes.description_pt: BackdoorDiplomacy é um grupo de ciberespionagem ativo desde pelo menos 2017. O BackdoorDiplomacy atacou ministérios das Relações Exteriores e empresas de telecomunicações na África, na Europa, no Oriente Médio e na Ásia.

nodes.name: Star Blizzard
nodes.description: Star Blizzard is a cyber espionage and influence group originating in Russia that has been active since at least 2019. Star Blizzard campaigns align closely with Russian state interests and have included persistent phishing and credential theft against academic, defense, government, NGO, and think tank organizations in NATO countries, particularly the US and the UK.
nodes.description_pt: Star Blizzard é um grupo de ciberespionagem e de operações de influência originário da Rússia, ativo desde pelo menos 2019. As campanhas do Star Blizzard estão fortemente alinhadas aos interesses do Estado russo e incluem phishing persistente e roubo de credenciais contra organizações acadêmicas, de defesa, governamentais, ONGs e think tanks em países da OTAN, em especial nos Estados Unidos e no Reino Unido.

nodes.name: Darkhotel
nodes.description: Darkhotel is a suspected South Korean threat group that has targeted victims primarily in East Asia since at least 2004. The group's name is based on cyber espionage operations conducted via hotel Internet networks against traveling executives and other select guests. Darkhotel has also conducted spearphishing campaigns and infected victims through peer-to-peer and file sharing networks.
nodes.description_pt: Darkhotel é um suposto grupo de ameaça sul-coreano que, desde pelo menos 2004, ataca vítimas principalmente no Leste Asiático. O nome do grupo se deve a operações de ciberespionagem conduzidas por meio de redes de internet de hotéis contra executivos em viagem e outros hóspedes selecionados. O Darkhotel também conduziu campanhas de spearphishing e infectou vítimas por meio de redes ponto a ponto (P2P) e de compartilhamento de arquivos.

nodes.name: Axiom
nodes.description: Axiom is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that has targeted the aerospace, defense, government, manufacturing, and media sectors since at least 2008. Some reporting suggests a degree of overlap between Axiom and Winnti Group but the two groups appear to be distinct based on differences in reporting on TTPs and targeting.
nodes.description_pt: Axiom é um suposto grupo chinês de ciberespionagem que, desde pelo menos 2008, ataca os setores aeroespacial, de defesa, governamental, industrial e de mídia. Alguns relatos sugerem certo grau de sobreposição entre o Axiom e o Winnti Group, mas os dois grupos parecem ser distintos, com base em diferenças nos relatos sobre TTPs e alvos.

nodes.name: TA578
nodes.description: TA578 is a threat actor that has used contact forms and email to initiate communications with victims and to distribute malware including Latrodectus, IcedID, and Bumblebee.
nodes.description_pt: TA578 é um ator de ameaça que utiliza formulários de contato e e-mails para iniciar comunicações com as vítimas e distribuir malwares como Latrodectus, IcedID e Bumblebee.

nodes.name: Deep Panda
nodes.description: Deep Panda is a suspected Chinese threat group known to target many industries, including government, defense, financial, and telecommunications. The intrusion into healthcare company Anthem has been attributed to Deep Panda. This group is also known as Shell Crew, WebMasters, KungFu Kittens, and PinkPanther. Deep Panda also appears to be known as Black Vine based on the attribution of both group names to the Anthem intrusion. Some analysts track Deep Panda and APT19 as the same group, but it is unclear from open source information if the groups are the same.
nodes.description_pt: Deep Panda é um suposto grupo de ameaça chinês conhecido por atacar diversos setores, incluindo governo, defesa, finanças e telecomunicações. A intrusão na operadora de saúde Anthem foi atribuída ao Deep Panda. O grupo também é conhecido como Shell Crew, WebMasters, KungFu Kittens e PinkPanther. O Deep Panda aparentemente também é conhecido como Black Vine, já que ambos os nomes foram atribuídos à intrusão na Anthem. Alguns analistas consideram o Deep Panda e o APT19 o mesmo grupo, mas as informações de fontes abertas não permitem confirmar essa equivalência.

nodes.name: Ember Bear
nodes.description: Ember Bear is a Russian state-sponsored cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2020, linked to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 161st Specialist Training Center (Unit 29155). Ember Bear has primarily focused operations against Ukrainian government and telecommunication entities, but has also operated against critical infrastructure entities in Europe and the Americas. Ember Bear conducted the WhisperGate destructive wiper attacks against Ukraine in early 2022. There is some confusion as to whether Ember Bear overlaps with another Russian-linked entity referred to as Saint Bear. At present available evidence strongly suggests these are distinct…
nodes.description_pt: Ember Bear é um grupo de ciberespionagem patrocinado pelo Estado russo, ativo desde pelo menos 2020 e ligado ao 161º Centro de Treinamento de Especialistas (Unidade 29155) da Diretoria Principal de Inteligência do Estado-Maior (GRU) da Rússia. O Ember Bear concentrou suas operações em entidades governamentais e de telecomunicações da Ucrânia, mas também atuou contra entidades de infraestrutura crítica na Europa e nas Américas. O grupo conduziu os ataques destrutivos com o wiper WhisperGate contra a Ucrânia no início de 2022. Há certa confusão sobre a sobreposição entre o Ember Bear e outra entidade ligada à Rússia, denominada Saint Bear. Atualmente, as evidências disponíveis indicam fortemente que se trata de agrupamentos distintos…

nodes.name: LazyScripter
nodes.description: LazyScripter is threat group that has mainly targeted the airlines industry since at least 2018, primarily using open-source toolsets.
nodes.description_pt: LazyScripter é um grupo de ameaça que, desde pelo menos 2018, ataca principalmente o setor aéreo, utilizando sobretudo conjuntos de ferramentas de código aberto.

nodes.name: Windshift
nodes.description: Windshift is a threat group that has been active since at least 2017, targeting specific individuals for surveillance in government departments and critical infrastructure across the Middle East.
nodes.description_pt: Windshift é um grupo de ameaça ativo desde pelo menos 2017, que vigia pessoas específicas em órgãos governamentais e em infraestrutura crítica no Oriente Médio.

nodes.name: Volatile Cedar
nodes.description: Volatile Cedar is a Lebanese threat group that has targeted individuals, companies, and institutions worldwide. Volatile Cedar has been operating since 2012 and is motivated by political and ideological interests.
nodes.description_pt: Volatile Cedar é um grupo de ameaça libanês que ataca pessoas, empresas e instituições em todo o mundo. O Volatile Cedar opera desde 2012 e é motivado por interesses políticos e ideológicos.

nodes.name: ToddyCat
nodes.description: ToddyCat is a sophisticated threat group that has been active since at least 2020 using custom loaders and malware in multi-stage infection chains against government and military targets across Europe and Asia.
nodes.description_pt: ToddyCat é um grupo de ameaça sofisticado, ativo desde pelo menos 2020, que utiliza carregadores (loaders) e malwares personalizados em cadeias de infecção de múltiplas etapas contra alvos governamentais e militares na Europa e na Ásia.

nodes.name: Whitefly
nodes.description: Whitefly is a cyber espionage group that has been operating since at least 2017. The group has targeted organizations based mostly in Singapore across a wide variety of sectors, and is primarily interested in stealing large amounts of sensitive information. The group has been linked to an attack against Singapore’s largest public health organization, SingHealth.
nodes.description_pt: Whitefly é um grupo de ciberespionagem em operação desde pelo menos 2017. O grupo ataca organizações sediadas principalmente em Singapura, de uma ampla variedade de setores, e tem como interesse principal o roubo de grandes volumes de informações sensíveis. O grupo foi associado a um ataque contra a maior organização de saúde pública de Singapura, a SingHealth.

nodes.name: LuminousMoth
nodes.description: LuminousMoth is a Chinese-speaking cyber espionage group that has been active since at least October 2020. LuminousMoth has targeted high-profile organizations, including government entities, in Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, and other parts of Southeast Asia. Some security researchers have concluded there is a connection between LuminousMoth and Mustang Panda based on similar targeting and TTPs, as well as network infrastructure overlaps.
nodes.description_pt: LuminousMoth é um grupo de ciberespionagem de língua chinesa, ativo desde pelo menos outubro de 2020. O LuminousMoth atacou organizações de alto perfil, incluindo entidades governamentais, em Mianmar, nas Filipinas, na Tailândia e em outras partes do Sudeste Asiático. Alguns pesquisadores de segurança concluíram que há conexão entre o LuminousMoth e o Mustang Panda, com base em alvos e TTPs semelhantes, além de sobreposições de infraestrutura de rede.

nodes.name: Agrius
nodes.description: Agrius is an Iranian threat actor active since 2020 notable for a series of ransomware and wiper operations in the Middle East, with an emphasis on Israeli targets. Public reporting has linked Agrius to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
nodes.description_pt: Agrius é um ator de ameaça iraniano, ativo desde 2020, conhecido por uma série de operações de ransomware e de wipers no Oriente Médio, com ênfase em alvos israelenses. Relatos públicos associam o Agrius ao Ministério de Inteligência e Segurança (MOIS) do Irã.

nodes.name: Water Galura
nodes.description: Water Galura are the operators of the Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) who handle payload generation, ransom negotiations, and the publication of stolen data for Qilin affilates recruited on Russian cybercrime forums. Water Galura have been active since at least 2022 and use a double extortion model where they demand payment for providing decryption keys and for refraining from publishing the stolen data to their leak site.
nodes.description_pt: Water Galura é o grupo operador do ransomware como serviço (RaaS) Qilin, responsável pela geração das cargas, pelas negociações de resgate e pela publicação dos dados roubados em nome dos afiliados do Qilin recrutados em fóruns cibercriminosos russos. Ativo desde pelo menos 2022, o Water Galura adota o modelo de dupla extorsão, exigindo pagamento tanto pelas chaves de decifração quanto para não publicar os dados roubados em seu site de vazamentos.

nodes.name: APT28
nodes.description: APT28 is a threat group that has been attributed to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 85th Main Special Service Center (GTsSS) military unit 26165. This group has been active since at least 2004.
nodes.description_pt: APT28 é um grupo de ameaça atribuído à unidade militar 26165 do 85º Centro Principal de Serviço Especial (GTsSS) da Diretoria Principal de Inteligência do Estado-Maior (GRU) da Rússia. O grupo está ativo desde pelo menos 2004.

nodes.name: Malteiro
nodes.description: Malteiro is a financially motivated criminal group that is likely based in Brazil and has been active since at least November 2019. The group operates and distributes the Mispadu banking trojan via a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) business model. Malteiro mainly targets victims throughout Latin America (particularly Mexico) and Europe (particularly Spain and Portugal).
nodes.description_pt: Malteiro é um grupo criminoso com motivação financeira, provavelmente sediado no Brasil e ativo desde pelo menos novembro de 2019. O grupo opera e distribui o trojan bancário Mispadu no modelo de malware como serviço (MaaS). O Malteiro ataca principalmente vítimas na América Latina (em especial no México) e na Europa (em especial na Espanha e em Portugal).

nodes.name: Metador
nodes.description: Metador is a suspected cyber espionage group that was first reported in September 2022. Metador has targeted a limited number of telecommunication companies, internet service providers, and universities in the Middle East and Africa. Security researchers named the group Metador based on the "I am meta" string in one of the group's malware samples and the expectation of Spanish-language responses from C2 servers.
nodes.description_pt: Metador é um suposto grupo de ciberespionagem relatado pela primeira vez em setembro de 2022. O Metador atacou um número limitado de empresas de telecomunicações, provedores de internet e universidades no Oriente Médio e na África. Pesquisadores de segurança deram ao grupo o nome Metador com base na string "I am meta", presente em uma das amostras de malware do grupo, e na expectativa de respostas em espanhol por parte dos servidores de C2.

nodes.name: APT42
nodes.description: APT42 is an Iranian-sponsored threat group that conducts cyber espionage and surveillance. The group primarily focuses on targets in the Middle East region, but has targeted a variety of industries and countries since at least 2015. APT42 starts cyber operations through spearphishing emails and/or the PINEFLOWER Android malware, then monitors and collects information from the compromised systems and devices. Finally, APT42 exfiltrates data using native features and open-source tools.
nodes.description_pt: APT42 é um grupo de ameaça patrocinado pelo Irã que conduz ciberespionagem e vigilância. O grupo concentra-se principalmente em alvos no Oriente Médio, mas, desde pelo menos 2015, atacou diversos setores e países. O APT42 inicia suas operações por meio de e-mails de spearphishing e/ou do malware para Android PINEFLOWER; em seguida, monitora e coleta informações dos sistemas e dispositivos comprometidos. Por fim, exfiltra os dados utilizando recursos nativos e ferramentas de código aberto.

nodes.name: APT5
nodes.description: APT5 is a China-based espionage actor that has been active since at least 2007 primarily targeting the telecommunications, aerospace, and defense industries throughout the U.S., Europe, and Asia. APT5 has displayed advanced tradecraft and significant interest in compromising networking devices and their underlying software including through the use of zero-day exploits.
nodes.description_pt: APT5 é um ator de espionagem sediado na China, ativo desde pelo menos 2007, que ataca principalmente os setores de telecomunicações, aeroespacial e de defesa nos Estados Unidos, na Europa e na Ásia. O APT5 demonstra técnicas avançadas e grande interesse em comprometer dispositivos de rede e seus softwares, inclusive por meio de explorações de dia zero.

nodes.name: Fox Kitten
nodes.description: Fox Kitten is threat actor with a suspected nexus to the Iranian government that has been active since at least 2017 against entities in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia, and North America. Fox Kitten has targeted multiple industrial verticals including oil and gas, technology, government, defense, healthcare, manufacturing, and engineering.
nodes.description_pt: Fox Kitten é um ator de ameaça com suspeita de vínculo com o governo iraniano, ativo desde pelo menos 2017 contra entidades no Oriente Médio, Norte da África, Europa, Austrália e América do Norte. O Fox Kitten atacou diversos setores, incluindo petróleo e gás, tecnologia, governo, defesa, saúde, indústria e engenharia.

nodes.name: RTM
nodes.description: RTM is a cybercriminal group that has been active since at least 2015 and is primarily interested in users of remote banking systems in Russia and neighboring countries. The group uses a Trojan by the same name (RTM).
nodes.description_pt: RTM é um grupo cibercriminoso ativo desde pelo menos 2015, interessado principalmente em usuários de sistemas de internet banking na Rússia e em países vizinhos. O grupo utiliza um trojan de mesmo nome (RTM).

nodes.name: APT12
nodes.description: APT12 is a threat group that has been attributed to China. The group has targeted a variety of victims including but not limited to media outlets, high-tech companies, and multiple governments.
nodes.description_pt: APT12 é um grupo de ameaça atribuído à China. O grupo atacou uma variedade de vítimas, incluindo, entre outros, veículos de comunicação, empresas de alta tecnologia e diversos governos.

nodes.name: APT-C-36
nodes.description: APT-C-36 is a suspected South American threat group that has engaged in espionage and financially motivated operations since at least 2018. APT-C-36 has targeted government institutions and entities in the financial, energy, and professional manufacturing sectors across Colombia and other Latin American countries.
nodes.description_pt: APT-C-36 é um suposto grupo de ameaça sul-americano que, desde pelo menos 2018, realiza operações de espionagem e com motivação financeira. O APT-C-36 atacou instituições governamentais e entidades dos setores financeiro, de energia e de manufatura na Colômbia e em outros países da América Latina.

nodes.name: Scarlet Mimic
nodes.description: Scarlet Mimic is a threat group that has targeted minority rights activists. This group has not been directly linked to a government source, but the group's motivations appear to overlap with those of the Chinese government. While there is some overlap between IP addresses used by Scarlet Mimic and Putter Panda, it has not been concluded that the groups are the same.
nodes.description_pt: Scarlet Mimic é um grupo de ameaça que ataca ativistas de direitos de minorias. O grupo não foi diretamente vinculado a uma fonte governamental, mas suas motivações parecem coincidir com as do governo chinês. Embora haja alguma sobreposição entre endereços IP utilizados pelo Scarlet Mimic e pelo Putter Panda, não se concluiu que sejam o mesmo grupo.

nodes.name: Winnti Group
nodes.description: Winnti Group is a threat group with Chinese origins that has been active since at least 2010. The group has heavily targeted the gaming industry, but it has also expanded the scope of its targeting. Some reporting suggests a number of other groups, including Axiom, APT17, and Ke3chang, are closely linked to Winnti Group.
nodes.description_pt: Winnti Group é um grupo de ameaça de origem chinesa, ativo desde pelo menos 2010. O grupo ataca intensamente a indústria de jogos eletrônicos, mas também ampliou o escopo de seus alvos. Alguns relatos sugerem que diversos outros grupos, incluindo Axiom, APT17 e Ke3chang, estão estreitamente ligados ao Winnti Group.

nodes.name: Tonto Team
nodes.description: Tonto Team is a suspected Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage threat group that has primarily targeted South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and the United States since at least 2009; by 2020 they expanded operations to include other Asian as well as Eastern European countries. Tonto Team has targeted government, military, energy, mining, financial, education, healthcare, and technology organizations, including through the Heartbeat Campaign (2009-2012) and Operation Bitter Biscuit (2017).
nodes.description_pt: Tonto Team é um suposto grupo de ciberespionagem patrocinado pelo Estado chinês que, desde pelo menos 2009, ataca principalmente a Coreia do Sul, o Japão, Taiwan e os Estados Unidos; em 2020, ampliou suas operações para outros países asiáticos e do Leste Europeu. O Tonto Team atacou organizações governamentais, militares, de energia, mineração, finanças, educação, saúde e tecnologia, inclusive por meio da Campanha Heartbeat (2009–2012) e da Operação Bitter Biscuit (2017).

nodes.name: GOLD SOUTHFIELD
nodes.description: GOLD SOUTHFIELD is a financially motivated threat group active since at least 2018 that operates the REvil Ransomware-as-a Service (RaaS). GOLD SOUTHFIELD provides backend infrastructure for affiliates recruited on underground forums to perpetrate high value deployments. By early 2020, GOLD SOUTHFIELD started capitalizing on the new trend of stealing data and further extorting the victim to pay for their data to not get publicly leaked.
nodes.description_pt: GOLD SOUTHFIELD é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira, ativo desde pelo menos 2018, que opera o ransomware como serviço (RaaS) REvil. O GOLD SOUTHFIELD fornece a infraestrutura de retaguarda para afiliados recrutados em fóruns clandestinos, que realizam implantações de alto valor. No início de 2020, o grupo passou a explorar a nova tendência de roubar dados e extorquir as vítimas para que pagassem a fim de evitar o vazamento público das informações.

nodes.name: Lazarus Group
nodes.description: Lazarus Group is a North Korean state-sponsored cyber threat group attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB). Lazarus Group has been active since at least 2009 and is reportedly responsible for the November 2014 destructive wiper attack on Sony Pictures Entertainment, identified by Novetta as part of Operation Blockbuster. Malware used by Lazarus Group correlates to other reported campaigns, including Operation Flame, Operation 1Mission, Operation Troy, DarkSeoul, and Ten Days of Rain.
nodes.description_pt: Lazarus Group é um grupo de ameaça cibernética patrocinado pelo Estado norte-coreano e atribuído ao Escritório Geral de Reconhecimento (RGB). Ativo desde pelo menos 2009, o Lazarus Group é apontado como responsável pelo ataque destrutivo com wiper contra a Sony Pictures Entertainment em novembro de 2014, identificado pela Novetta como parte da Operação Blockbuster. Os malwares usados pelo Lazarus Group estão relacionados a outras campanhas relatadas, incluindo a Operação Flame, a Operação 1Mission, a Operação Troy, DarkSeoul e Ten Days of Rain.

nodes.name: INC Ransom
nodes.description: INC Ransom is a ransomware and data extortion threat group associated with the deployment of INC Ransomware that has been active since at least July 2023. INC Ransom has targeted organizations worldwide most commonly in the industrial, healthcare, and education sectors in the US and Europe.
nodes.description_pt: INC Ransom é um grupo de ameaça de ransomware e extorsão de dados associado à implantação do INC Ransomware, ativo desde pelo menos julho de 2023. O INC Ransom ataca organizações em todo o mundo, com maior frequência nos setores industrial, de saúde e de educação nos Estados Unidos e na Europa.

nodes.name: Earth Lusca
nodes.description: Earth Lusca is a suspected China-based cyber espionage group that has been active since at least April 2019. Earth Lusca has targeted organizations in Australia, China, Hong Kong, Mongolia, Nepal, the Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Arab Emirates, Nigeria, Germany, France, and the United States. Targets included government institutions, news media outlets, gambling companies, educational institutions, COVID-19 research organizations, telecommunications companies, religious movements banned in China, and cryptocurrency trading platforms; security researchers assess some Earth Lusca operations may be financially motivated.
nodes.description_pt: Earth Lusca é um suposto grupo de ciberespionagem sediado na China, ativo desde pelo menos abril de 2019. O Earth Lusca atacou organizações na Austrália, China, Hong Kong, Mongólia, Nepal, Filipinas, Taiwan, Tailândia, Vietnã, Emirados Árabes Unidos, Nigéria, Alemanha, França e Estados Unidos. Entre os alvos estão instituições governamentais, veículos de comunicação, empresas de apostas, instituições de ensino, organizações de pesquisa sobre a COVID-19, empresas de telecomunicações, movimentos religiosos proibidos na China e plataformas de negociação de criptomoedas; pesquisadores de segurança avaliam que algumas operações do Earth Lusca podem ter motivação financeira.

nodes.name: FIN4
nodes.description: FIN4 is a financially-motivated threat group that has targeted confidential information related to the public financial market, particularly regarding healthcare and pharmaceutical companies, since at least 2013. FIN4 is unique in that they do not infect victims with typical persistent malware, but rather they focus on capturing credentials authorized to access email and other non-public correspondence.
nodes.description_pt: FIN4 é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira que, desde pelo menos 2013, busca informações confidenciais relacionadas ao mercado financeiro, em especial sobre empresas de saúde e farmacêuticas. O FIN4 se diferencia por não infectar as vítimas com o típico malware persistente; em vez disso, concentra-se em capturar credenciais autorizadas a acessar e-mails e outras correspondências não públicas.

nodes.name: Silence
nodes.description: Silence is a financially motivated threat actor targeting financial institutions in different countries. The group was first seen in June 2016. Their main targets reside in Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Azerbaijan, Poland and Kazakhstan. They compromised various banking systems, including the Russian Central Bank's Automated Workstation Client, ATMs, and card processing.
nodes.description_pt: Silence é um ator de ameaça com motivação financeira que ataca instituições financeiras em diversos países. O grupo foi observado pela primeira vez em junho de 2016. Seus principais alvos estão na Rússia, Ucrânia, Belarus, Azerbaijão, Polônia e Cazaquistão. O grupo comprometeu diversos sistemas bancários, incluindo o cliente de estação de trabalho automatizada do Banco Central da Rússia, caixas eletrônicos e sistemas de processamento de cartões.

nodes.name: Sowbug
nodes.description: Sowbug is a threat group that has conducted targeted attacks against organizations in South America and Southeast Asia, particularly government entities, since at least 2015.
nodes.description_pt: Sowbug é um grupo de ameaça que, desde pelo menos 2015, conduz ataques direcionados contra organizações na América do Sul e no Sudeste Asiático, em especial entidades governamentais.

nodes.name: Threat Group-1314
nodes.description: Threat Group-1314 is an unattributed threat group that has used compromised credentials to log into a victim's remote access infrastructure.
nodes.description_pt: Threat Group-1314 é um grupo de ameaça sem atribuição definida, que utilizou credenciais comprometidas para acessar a infraestrutura de acesso remoto das vítimas.

nodes.name: Thrip
nodes.description: Thrip is an espionage group that has targeted satellite communications, telecoms, and defense contractor companies in the U.S. and Southeast Asia. The group uses custom malware as well as "living off the land" techniques.
nodes.description_pt: Thrip é um grupo de espionagem que ataca empresas de comunicação via satélite, de telecomunicações e fornecedoras do setor de defesa nos Estados Unidos e no Sudeste Asiático. O grupo utiliza malware personalizado e técnicas baseadas em recursos nativos do sistema (living off the land).

nodes.name: APT16
nodes.description: APT16 is a China-based threat group that has launched spearphishing campaigns targeting Japanese and Taiwanese organizations.
nodes.description_pt: APT16 é um grupo de ameaça sediado na China que lançou campanhas de spearphishing contra organizações japonesas e taiwanesas.

nodes.name: LAPSUS$
nodes.description: LAPSUS$ is cyber criminal threat group that has been active since at least mid-2021. LAPSUS$ specializes in large-scale social engineering and extortion operations, including destructive attacks without the use of ransomware. The group has targeted organizations globally, including in the government, manufacturing, higher education, energy, healthcare, technology, telecommunications, and media sectors.
nodes.description_pt: LAPSUS$ é um grupo cibercriminoso ativo desde pelo menos meados de 2021. O LAPSUS$ é especializado em operações de engenharia social e extorsão em larga escala, incluindo ataques destrutivos sem uso de ransomware. O grupo atacou organizações em todo o mundo, incluindo os setores governamental, industrial, de ensino superior, energia, saúde, tecnologia, telecomunicações e mídia.

nodes.name: BlackOasis
nodes.description: BlackOasis is a Middle Eastern threat group that is believed to be a customer of Gamma Group. The group has shown interest in prominent figures in the United Nations, as well as opposition bloggers, activists, regional news correspondents, and think tanks. A group known by Microsoft as NEODYMIUM is reportedly associated closely with BlackOasis operations, but evidence that the group names are aliases has not been identified.
nodes.description_pt: BlackOasis é um grupo de ameaça do Oriente Médio que, supostamente, é cliente do Gamma Group. O grupo demonstrou interesse em figuras proeminentes das Nações Unidas, bem como em blogueiros de oposição, ativistas, correspondentes de notícias regionais e think tanks. Há relatos de que um grupo chamado NEODYMIUM pela Microsoft esteja estreitamente associado às operações do BlackOasis, mas não foram identificadas evidências de que os nomes sejam sinônimos.

nodes.name: Cobalt Group
nodes.description: Cobalt Group is a financially motivated threat group that has primarily targeted financial institutions since at least 2016. The group has conducted intrusions to steal money via targeting ATM systems, card processing, payment systems and SWIFT systems. Cobalt Group has mainly targeted banks in Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia. One of the alleged leaders was arrested in Spain in early 2018, but the group still appears to be active. The group has been known to target organizations in order to use their access to then compromise additional victims. Reporting indicates there may be links between Cobalt Group and both the malware Carbanak and the group Carbanak.
nodes.description_pt: Cobalt Group é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira que, desde pelo menos 2016, ataca principalmente instituições financeiras. O grupo realizou intrusões para roubar dinheiro atacando sistemas de caixas eletrônicos, processamento de cartões, sistemas de pagamento e sistemas SWIFT. O Cobalt Group ataca principalmente bancos no Leste Europeu, na Ásia Central e no Sudeste Asiático. Um dos supostos líderes foi preso na Espanha no início de 2018, mas o grupo aparentemente continua ativo. O grupo é conhecido por atacar organizações para usar o acesso obtido e, a partir dele, comprometer outras vítimas. Relatos indicam possíveis ligações entre o Cobalt Group, o malware Carbanak e o grupo Carbanak.

nodes.name: CopyKittens
nodes.description: CopyKittens is an Iranian cyber espionage group that has been operating since at least 2013. It has targeted countries including Israel, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, the U.S., Jordan, and Germany. The group is responsible for the campaign known as Operation Wilted Tulip.
nodes.description_pt: CopyKittens é um grupo iraniano de ciberespionagem em operação desde pelo menos 2013. O grupo atacou países como Israel, Arábia Saudita, Turquia, Estados Unidos, Jordânia e Alemanha, e é responsável pela campanha conhecida como Operação Wilted Tulip.

nodes.name: Wizard Spider
nodes.description: Wizard Spider is a Russia-based financially motivated threat group originally known for the creation and deployment of TrickBot since at least 2016. Wizard Spider possesses a diverse arsenal of tools and has conducted ransomware campaigns against a variety of organizations, ranging from major corporations to hospitals.
nodes.description_pt: Wizard Spider é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira sediado na Rússia, originalmente conhecido pela criação e implantação do TrickBot desde pelo menos 2016. O Wizard Spider possui um arsenal diversificado de ferramentas e conduziu campanhas de ransomware contra diversas organizações, de grandes corporações a hospitais.

nodes.name: Molerats
nodes.description: Molerats is an Arabic-speaking, politically-motivated threat group that has been operating since 2012. The group's victims have primarily been in the Middle East, Europe, and the United States.
nodes.description_pt: Molerats é um grupo de ameaça de língua árabe e com motivação política, em operação desde 2012. As vítimas do grupo estão principalmente no Oriente Médio, na Europa e nos Estados Unidos.

nodes.name: Velvet Ant
nodes.description: Velvet Ant is a threat actor operating since at least 2021. Velvet Ant is associated with complex persistence mechanisms, the targeting of network devices and appliances during operations, and the use of zero day exploits.
nodes.description_pt: Velvet Ant é um ator de ameaça em operação desde pelo menos 2021. O Velvet Ant está associado a mecanismos complexos de persistência, ao ataque a dispositivos e appliances de rede e ao uso de explorações de dia zero.

nodes.name: Transparent Tribe
nodes.description: Transparent Tribe is a suspected Pakistan-based threat group that has been active since at least 2013, primarily targeting diplomatic, defense, and research organizations in India and Afghanistan.
nodes.description_pt: Transparent Tribe é um suposto grupo de ameaça sediado no Paquistão, ativo desde pelo menos 2013, que ataca principalmente organizações diplomáticas, de defesa e de pesquisa na Índia e no Afeganistão.

nodes.name: IndigoZebra
nodes.description: IndigoZebra is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that has been targeting Central Asian governments since at least 2014.
nodes.description_pt: IndigoZebra é um suposto grupo chinês de ciberespionagem que, desde pelo menos 2014, ataca governos da Ásia Central.

nodes.name: Moonstone Sleet
nodes.description: Moonstone Sleet is a North Korean-linked threat actor executing both financially motivated attacks and espionage operations. The group previously overlapped significantly with another North Korean-linked entity, Lazarus Group, but has differentiated its tradecraft since 2023. Moonstone Sleet is notable for creating fake companies and personas to interact with victim entities, as well as developing unique malware such as a variant delivered via a fully functioning game.
nodes.description_pt: Moonstone Sleet é um ator de ameaça ligado à Coreia do Norte que executa tanto ataques com motivação financeira quanto operações de espionagem. O grupo já se sobrepôs significativamente a outra entidade ligada à Coreia do Norte, o Lazarus Group, mas diferenciou suas técnicas a partir de 2023. O Moonstone Sleet destaca-se pela criação de empresas e personas falsas para interagir com as vítimas, bem como pelo desenvolvimento de malwares próprios, como uma variante distribuída por meio de um jogo totalmente funcional.

nodes.name: Inception
nodes.description: Inception is a cyber espionage group active since at least 2014. The group has targeted multiple industries and governmental entities primarily in Russia, but has also been active in the United States and throughout Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
nodes.description_pt: Inception é um grupo de ciberespionagem ativo desde pelo menos 2014. O grupo atacou diversos setores e entidades governamentais, principalmente na Rússia, mas também atuou nos Estados Unidos e em toda a Europa, Ásia, África e Oriente Médio.

nodes.name: VOID MANTICORE
nodes.description: VOID MANTICORE is a threat group assessed to operate on behalf of Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Active since at least mid-2022, VOID MANTICORE has targeted government entities, critical infrastructure, and private sector organizations across Albania, Israel, and the United States. VOID MANTICORE conducts destructive cyber operations, combining wiper attacks with hack-and-leak campaigns. The group has operated under multiple public-facing personas, including HomeLand Justice in operations against Albania, Karma and Karma Below in campaigns targeting Israeli organizations, and Handala Hack, its current primary persona, which has claimed activity against Israeli and U.S.…
nodes.description_pt: VOID MANTICORE é um grupo de ameaça avaliado como atuante em nome do Ministério de Inteligência e Segurança (MOIS) do Irã. Ativo desde pelo menos meados de 2022, o VOID MANTICORE atacou entidades governamentais, infraestrutura crítica e organizações do setor privado na Albânia, em Israel e nos Estados Unidos. O grupo conduz operações cibernéticas destrutivas, combinando ataques com wipers e campanhas de invasão e vazamento (hack-and-leak). O grupo atuou sob diversas personas públicas, incluindo HomeLand Justice, nas operações contra a Albânia; Karma e Karma Below, nas campanhas contra organizações israelenses; e Handala Hack, sua principal persona atual, que reivindicou atividades contra alvos israelenses e norte-americanos…

nodes.name: Play
nodes.description: Play is a ransomware group that has been active since at least 2022 deploying Playcrypt ransomware against the business, government, critical infrastructure, healthcare, and media sectors in North America, South America, and Europe. Play actors employ a double-extortion model, encrypting systems after exfiltrating data, and are presumed by security researchers to operate as a closed group.
nodes.description_pt: Play é um grupo de ransomware ativo desde pelo menos 2022, que implanta o ransomware Playcrypt contra os setores empresarial, governamental, de infraestrutura crítica, saúde e mídia na América do Norte, na América do Sul e na Europa. Os operadores do Play adotam o modelo de dupla extorsão, criptografando os sistemas após exfiltrar os dados, e pesquisadores de segurança presumem que operem como um grupo fechado.

nodes.name: PROMETHIUM
nodes.description: PROMETHIUM is an activity group focused on espionage that has been active since at least 2012. The group has conducted operations globally with a heavy emphasis on Turkish targets. PROMETHIUM has demonstrated similarity to another activity group called NEODYMIUM due to overlapping victim and campaign characteristics.
nodes.description_pt: PROMETHIUM é um grupo de atividade voltado à espionagem, ativo desde pelo menos 2012. O grupo conduziu operações em todo o mundo, com forte ênfase em alvos turcos. O PROMETHIUM apresenta semelhanças com outro grupo de atividade, denominado NEODYMIUM, em razão da sobreposição de vítimas e de características de campanha.

nodes.name: APT30
nodes.description: APT30 is a threat group suspected to be associated with the Chinese government. While Naikon shares some characteristics with APT30, the two groups do not appear to be exact matches.
nodes.description_pt: APT30 é um grupo de ameaça supostamente associado ao governo chinês. Embora o Naikon compartilhe algumas características com o APT30, os dois grupos não parecem ser exatamente o mesmo.

nodes.name: HEXANE
nodes.description: HEXANE is a cyber espionage threat group that has targeted oil & gas, telecommunications, aviation, and internet service provider organizations since at least 2017. Targeted companies have been located in the Middle East and Africa, including Israel, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Morocco, and Tunisia. HEXANE's TTPs appear similar to APT33 and OilRig but due to differences in victims and tools it is tracked as a separate entity.
nodes.description_pt: HEXANE é um grupo de ciberespionagem que, desde pelo menos 2017, ataca organizações de petróleo e gás, telecomunicações, aviação e provedores de internet. As empresas atacadas estão localizadas no Oriente Médio e na África, incluindo Israel, Arábia Saudita, Kuwait, Marrocos e Tunísia. As TTPs do HEXANE se assemelham às do APT33 e do OilRig, mas, em razão de diferenças nas vítimas e nas ferramentas, o grupo é rastreado como entidade separada.

nodes.name: DragonOK
nodes.description: DragonOK is a threat group that has targeted Japanese organizations with phishing emails. Due to overlapping TTPs, including similar custom tools, DragonOK is thought to have a direct or indirect relationship with the threat group Moafee. It is known to use a variety of malware, including Sysget/HelloBridge, PlugX, PoisonIvy, FormerFirstRat, NFlog, and NewCT.
nodes.description_pt: DragonOK é um grupo de ameaça que ataca organizações japonesas com e-mails de phishing. Em razão da sobreposição de TTPs, incluindo ferramentas personalizadas semelhantes, acredita-se que o DragonOK tenha relação direta ou indireta com o grupo de ameaça Moafee. O grupo é conhecido por utilizar diversos malwares, incluindo Sysget/HelloBridge, PlugX, PoisonIvy, FormerFirstRat, NFlog e NewCT.

nodes.name: Daggerfly
nodes.description: Daggerfly is a People's Republic of China-linked APT entity active since at least 2012. Daggerfly has targeted individuals, government and NGO entities, and telecommunication companies in Asia and Africa. Daggerfly is associated with exclusive use of MgBot malware and is noted for several potential supply chain infection campaigns.
nodes.description_pt: Daggerfly é uma entidade APT ligada à República Popular da China, ativa desde pelo menos 2012. O Daggerfly atacou pessoas, entidades governamentais, ONGs e empresas de telecomunicações na Ásia e na África. O grupo está associado ao uso exclusivo do malware MgBot e é conhecido por diversas possíveis campanhas de infecção pela cadeia de suprimentos.

nodes.name: Rancor
nodes.description: Rancor is a threat group that has led targeted campaigns against the South East Asia region. Rancor uses politically-motivated lures to entice victims to open malicious documents.
nodes.description_pt: Rancor é um grupo de ameaça que conduziu campanhas direcionadas contra o Sudeste Asiático. O Rancor utiliza iscas de cunho político para induzir as vítimas a abrir documentos maliciosos.

nodes.name: WIRTE
nodes.description: WIRTE is a cyberespionage actor, believed to be a subgroup of the Hamas-affiliated Gaza Cybergang, that has been active since at least August 2018. WIRTE has targeted diplomatic, financial, military, legal, and technology organizations across the Middle East, North Africa, and in Europe to gather intelligence. WIRTE has remained persistently active despite the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict and has expanded their operations to include wiper malware attacks against Israeli targets.
nodes.description_pt: WIRTE é um ator de ciberespionagem, considerado um subgrupo do Gaza Cybergang, afiliado ao Hamas, e ativo desde pelo menos agosto de 2018. O WIRTE atacou organizações diplomáticas, financeiras, militares, jurídicas e de tecnologia no Oriente Médio, no Norte da África e na Europa para coletar inteligência. O WIRTE manteve-se ativo de forma persistente, apesar do conflito entre Israel e o Hamas, e ampliou suas operações para incluir ataques com wipers contra alvos israelenses.

nodes.name: PLATINUM
nodes.description: PLATINUM is an activity group that has targeted victims since at least 2009. The group has focused on targets associated with governments and related organizations in South and Southeast Asia.
nodes.description_pt: PLATINUM é um grupo de atividade que ataca vítimas desde pelo menos 2009. O grupo concentra-se em alvos ligados a governos e organizações relacionadas no Sul e no Sudeste Asiático.

nodes.name: Magic Hound
nodes.description: Magic Hound is an Iranian-sponsored threat group that conducts long term, resource-intensive cyber espionage operations, likely on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. They have targeted European, U.S., and Middle Eastern government and military personnel, academics, journalists, and organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO), via complex social engineering campaigns since at least 2014.
nodes.description_pt: Magic Hound é um grupo de ameaça patrocinado pelo Irã que conduz operações de ciberespionagem de longo prazo e uso intensivo de recursos, provavelmente em nome do Corpo da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica. Desde pelo menos 2014, o grupo ataca funcionários governamentais e militares da Europa, dos Estados Unidos e do Oriente Médio, acadêmicos, jornalistas e organizações como a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), por meio de campanhas complexas de engenharia social.

nodes.name: Ajax Security Team
nodes.description: Ajax Security Team is a group that has been active since at least 2010 and believed to be operating out of Iran. By 2014 Ajax Security Team transitioned from website defacement operations to malware-based cyber espionage campaigns targeting the US defense industrial base and Iranian users of anti-censorship technologies.
nodes.description_pt: Ajax Security Team é um grupo ativo desde pelo menos 2010, que supostamente opera a partir do Irã. Em 2014, o Ajax Security Team passou de operações de desfiguração de sites para campanhas de ciberespionagem baseadas em malware, voltadas à base industrial de defesa dos Estados Unidos e a usuários iranianos de tecnologias anticensura.

nodes.name: Threat Group-3390
nodes.description: Threat Group-3390 is a Chinese threat group that has extensively used strategic Web compromises to target victims. The group has been active since at least 2010 and has targeted organizations in the aerospace, government, defense, technology, energy, manufacturing and gambling/betting sectors.
nodes.description_pt: Threat Group-3390 é um grupo de ameaça chinês que utilizou amplamente o comprometimento estratégico de sites para atingir suas vítimas. Ativo desde pelo menos 2010, o grupo atacou organizações dos setores aeroespacial, governamental, de defesa, tecnologia, energia, indústria e jogos de azar/apostas.

nodes.name: APT33
nodes.description: APT33 is a suspected Iranian threat group that has carried out operations since at least 2013. The group has targeted organizations across multiple industries in the United States, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea, with a particular interest in the aviation and energy sectors.
nodes.description_pt: APT33 é um suposto grupo de ameaça iraniano que realiza operações desde pelo menos 2013. O grupo atacou organizações de diversos setores nos Estados Unidos, na Arábia Saudita e na Coreia do Sul, com interesse especial nos setores de aviação e energia.

nodes.name: FIN10
nodes.description: FIN10 is a financially motivated threat group that has targeted organizations in North America since at least 2013 through 2016. The group uses stolen data exfiltrated from victims to extort organizations.
nodes.description_pt: FIN10 é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira que atacou organizações na América do Norte entre, pelo menos, 2013 e 2016. O grupo utiliza dados roubados e exfiltrados das vítimas para extorquir as organizações.

nodes.name: FIN8
nodes.description: FIN8 is a financially motivated threat group that has been active since at least January 2016, and known for targeting organizations in the hospitality, retail, entertainment, insurance, technology, chemical, and financial sectors. In June 2021, security researchers detected FIN8 switching from targeting point-of-sale (POS) devices to distributing a number of ransomware variants.
nodes.description_pt: FIN8 é um grupo de ameaça com motivação financeira, ativo desde pelo menos janeiro de 2016 e conhecido por atacar organizações dos setores de hotelaria, varejo, entretenimento, seguros, tecnologia, químico e financeiro. Em junho de 2021, pesquisadores de segurança identificaram que o FIN8 deixou de atacar dispositivos de ponto de venda (PDV) para distribuir diversas variantes de ransomware.

nodes.name: FIN13
nodes.description: FIN13 is a financially motivated cyber threat group that has targeted the financial, retail, and hospitality industries in Mexico and Latin America, as early as 2016. FIN13 achieves its objectives by stealing intellectual property, financial data, mergers and acquisition information, or PII.
nodes.description_pt: FIN13 é um grupo de ameaça cibernética com motivação financeira que, desde 2016, ataca os setores financeiro, de varejo e de hotelaria no México e na América Latina. O FIN13 atinge seus objetivos roubando propriedade intelectual, dados financeiros, informações sobre fusões e aquisições ou informações de identificação pessoal.

nodes.name: APT19
nodes.description: APT19 is a Chinese-based threat group that has targeted a variety of industries, including defense, finance, energy, pharmaceutical, telecommunications, high tech, education, manufacturing, and legal services. In 2017, a phishing campaign was used to target seven law and investment firms. Some analysts track APT19 and Deep Panda as the same group, but it is unclear from open source information if the groups are the same.
nodes.description_pt: APT19 é um grupo de ameaça sediado na China que atacou diversos setores, incluindo defesa, finanças, energia, farmacêutico, telecomunicações, alta tecnologia, educação, indústria e serviços jurídicos. Em 2017, uma campanha de phishing foi utilizada contra sete escritórios de advocacia e empresas de investimento. Alguns analistas consideram o APT19 e o Deep Panda o mesmo grupo, mas as informações de fontes abertas não permitem confirmar essa equivalência.

nodes.name: PittyTiger
nodes.description: PittyTiger is a threat group believed to operate out of China that uses multiple different types of malware to maintain command and control.
nodes.description_pt: PittyTiger é um grupo de ameaça que supostamente opera a partir da China e utiliza diversos tipos de malware para manter o comando e controle.

nodes.name: Nomadic Octopus
nodes.description: Nomadic Octopus is a Russian-speaking cyber espionage threat group that has primarily targeted Central Asia, including local governments, diplomatic missions, and individuals, since at least 2014. Nomadic Octopus has been observed conducting campaigns involving Android and Windows malware, mainly using the Delphi programming language, and building custom variants.
nodes.description_pt: Nomadic Octopus é um grupo de ciberespionagem de língua russa que, desde pelo menos 2014, ataca principalmente a Ásia Central, incluindo governos locais, missões diplomáticas e pessoas físicas. O Nomadic Octopus foi observado conduzindo campanhas com malwares para Android e Windows, desenvolvidos principalmente na linguagem Delphi, e criando variantes personalizadas.

nodes.name: HDoor
nodes.description: HDoor is malware that has been customized and used by the Naikon group.

nodes.name: TrickBot
nodes.description: TrickBot is a Trojan spyware program written in C++ that first emerged in September 2016 as a possible successor to Dyre. TrickBot was developed and initially used by Wizard Spider for targeting banking sites in North America, Australia, and throughout Europe; it has since been used against all sectors worldwide as part of "big game hunting" ransomware campaigns.

nodes.name: cd00r
nodes.description: cd00r is an open-source backdoor for UNIX and UNIX-variant operating systems that was orginally released in 2000. cd00r source code is primarily based on a packet-capturing program as it utilizes a sniffer to listen for specific sequences of network traffic or "secret knock" before executing the attacker's code.

nodes.name: PowerDuke
nodes.description: PowerDuke is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2016. It has primarily been delivered through Microsoft Word or Excel attachments containing malicious macros.

nodes.name: EKANS
nodes.description: EKANS is ransomware variant written in Golang that first appeared in mid-December 2019 and has been used against multiple sectors, including energy, healthcare, and automotive manufacturing, which in some cases resulted in significant operational disruptions. EKANS has used a hard-coded kill-list of processes, including some associated with common ICS software platforms (e.g., GE Proficy, Honeywell HMIWeb, etc), similar to those defined in MegaCortex.

nodes.name: BLINDINGCAN
nodes.description: BLINDINGCAN is a remote access Trojan that has been used by the North Korean government since at least early 2020 in cyber operations against defense, engineering, and government organizations in Western Europe and the US.

nodes.name: Ninja
nodes.description: Ninja is a malware developed in C++ that has been used by ToddyCat to penetrate networks and control remote systems since at least 2020. Ninja is possibly part of a post exploitation toolkit exclusively used by ToddyCat and allows multiple operators to work simultaneously on the same machine. Ninja has been used against government and military entities in Europe and Asia and observed in specific infection chains being deployed by Samurai.

nodes.name: Pikabot
nodes.description: Pikabot is a backdoor used for initial access and follow-on tool deployment active since early 2023. Pikabot is notable for extensive use of multiple encoding, encryption, and defense evasion mechanisms to evade defenses and avoid analysis. Pikabot has some overlaps with QakBot, but insufficient evidence exists to definitively link these two malware families. Pikabot is frequently used to deploy follow on tools such as Cobalt Strike or ransomware variants.

nodes.name: Wiarp
nodes.description: Wiarp is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

nodes.name: RCSession
nodes.description: RCSession is a backdoor written in C++ that has been in use since at least 2018 by Mustang Panda and by Threat Group-3390 (Type II Backdoor).

nodes.name: Spark
nodes.description: Spark is a Windows backdoor and has been in use since as early as 2017.

nodes.name: QuietSieve
nodes.description: QuietSieve is an information stealer that has been used by Gamaredon Group since at least 2021.

nodes.name: SynAck
nodes.description: SynAck is variant of Trojan ransomware targeting mainly English-speaking users since at least fall 2017.

nodes.name: Bumblebee
nodes.description: Bumblebee is a custom loader written in C++ that has been used by multiple threat actors, including possible initial access brokers, to download and execute additional payloads since at least March 2022. Bumblebee has been linked to ransomware operations including Conti, Quantum, and Mountlocker and derived its name from the appearance of "bumblebee" in the user-agent.

nodes.name: BRICKSTORM
nodes.description: BRICKSTORM is a cross-platform backdoor with variants written in Go and Rust that facilitates command and control, the ingress transfer of other malware, and the exfiltration of data. BRICKSTORM has also been created from a .NET application using ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation to blend in within victim environments. BRICKSTORM was first observed in April 2024. BRICKSTORM has previously been leveraged by People's Republic of China (PRC) state-nexus actors identified as UNC6201, UNC5221, WARP PANDA, PunyToad, and SYLVANITE.

nodes.name: MURKYTOP
nodes.description: MURKYTOP is a reconnaissance tool used by Leviathan.

nodes.name: AcidRain
nodes.description: AcidRain is an ELF binary targeting modems and routers using MIPS architecture. AcidRain is associated with the ViaSat KA-SAT communication outage that took place during the initial phases of the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Analysis indicates overlap with another network device-targeting malware, VPNFilter, associated with Sandworm Team. US and European government sources linked AcidRain to Russian government entities, while Ukrainian government sources linked AcidRain specifically to Sandworm Team.

nodes.name: GRIFFON
nodes.description: GRIFFON is a JavaScript backdoor used by FIN7.

nodes.name: Exaramel for Windows
nodes.description: Exaramel for Windows is a backdoor used for targeting Windows systems. The Linux version is tracked separately under Exaramel for Linux.

nodes.name: Amadey
nodes.description: Amadey is a Trojan bot that has been used since at least October 2018.

nodes.name: JumbledPath
nodes.description: JumbledPath is a custom-built utility written in GO that has been used by Salt Typhoon since at least 2024 for packet capture on remote Cisco devices. JumbledPath is compiled as an ELF binary using x86-64 architecture which makes it potentially useable across Linux operating systems and network devices from multiple vendors.

nodes.name: RDFSNIFFER
nodes.description: RDFSNIFFER is a module loaded by BOOSTWRITE which allows an attacker to monitor and tamper with legitimate connections made via an application designed to provide visibility and system management capabilities to remote IT techs.

nodes.name: NICECURL
nodes.description: NICECURL is a VBScript-based backdoor used by APT42 to download additional modules.

nodes.name: Proxysvc
nodes.description: Proxysvc is a malicious DLL used by Lazarus Group in a campaign known as Operation GhostSecret. It has appeared to be operating undetected since 2017 and was mostly observed in higher education organizations. The goal of Proxysvc is to deliver additional payloads to the target and to maintain control for the attacker. It is in the form of a DLL that can also be executed as a standalone process.

nodes.name: Orz
nodes.description: Orz is a custom JavaScript backdoor used by Leviathan. It was observed being used in 2014 as well as in August 2017 when it was dropped by Microsoft Publisher files.

nodes.name: Torisma
nodes.description: Torisma is a second stage implant designed for specialized monitoring that has been used by Lazarus Group. Torisma was discovered during an investigation into the 2020 Operation North Star campaign that targeted the defense sector.

nodes.name: NOKKI
nodes.description: NOKKI is a modular remote access tool. The earliest observed attack using NOKKI was in January 2018. NOKKI has significant code overlap with the KONNI malware family. There is some evidence potentially linking NOKKI to APT37.

nodes.name: yty
nodes.description: yty is a modular, plugin-based malware framework. The components of the framework are written in a variety of programming languages.

nodes.name: Backdoor.Oldrea
nodes.description: Backdoor.Oldrea is a modular backdoor that used by Dragonfly against energy companies since at least 2013. Backdoor.Oldrea was distributed via supply chain compromise, and included specialized modules to enumerate and map ICS-specific systems, processes, and protocols.

nodes.name: DOGCALL
nodes.description: DOGCALL is a backdoor used by APT37 that has been used to target South Korean government and military organizations in 2017. It is typically dropped using a Hangul Word Processor (HWP) exploit.

nodes.name: Stuxnet
nodes.description: Stuxnet was the first publicly reported malware to specifically target industrial control systems devices. Stuxnet is a large and complex malware that utilized multiple behaviors, including numerous zero-day vulnerabilities, a sophisticated Windows rootkit, and network infection routines. Stuxnet was discovered in 2010, with some components being used as early as November 2008.

nodes.name: IronWind
nodes.description: IronWind is a custom loader malware that has been in use since at least 2023 by actors including WIRTE to target entities in the Middle East.

nodes.name: Downdelph
nodes.description: Downdelph is a first-stage downloader written in Delphi that has been used by APT28 in rare instances between 2013 and 2015.

nodes.name: RotaJakiro
nodes.description: RotaJakiro is a 64-bit Linux backdoor used by APT32. First seen in 2018, it uses a plugin architecture to extend capabilities. RotaJakiro can determine it's permission level and execute according to access type (`root` or `user`).

nodes.name: AvosLocker
nodes.description: AvosLocker is ransomware written in C++ that has been offered via the Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model. It was first observed in June 2021 and has been used against financial services, critical manufacturing, government facilities, and other critical infrastructure sectors in the United States. As of March 2022, AvosLocker had also been used against organizations in Belgium, Canada, China, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Syria, Taiwan, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom.

nodes.name: SEASHARPEE
nodes.description: SEASHARPEE is a Web shell that has been used by OilRig.

nodes.name: Get2
nodes.description: Get2 is a downloader written in C++ that has been used by TA505 to deliver FlawedGrace, FlawedAmmyy, Snatch and SDBbot.

nodes.name: POWRUNER
nodes.description: POWRUNER is a PowerShell script that sends and receives commands to and from the C2 server.

nodes.name: KOPILUWAK
nodes.description: KOPILUWAK is a JavaScript-based reconnaissance tool that has been used for victim profiling and C2 since at least 2017.

nodes.name: RobbinHood
nodes.description: RobbinHood is ransomware that was first observed being used in an attack against the Baltimore city government's computer network.

nodes.name: MEDUSA
nodes.description: MEDUSA is an open-source rootkit that is capable of dynamic linker hijacking, command execution, and logging credentials.

nodes.name: VersaMem
nodes.description: VersaMem is a web shell designed for deployment to Versa Director servers following exploitation. Discovered in August 2024, VersaMem was used during Versa Director Zero Day Exploitation by Volt Typhoon to target ISPs and MSPs. VersaMem is deployed as a Java Archive (JAR) and allows for credential capture for Versa Director logon activity as well as follow-on execution of arbitrary Java payloads.

nodes.name: Power Loader
nodes.description: Power Loader is modular code sold in the cybercrime market used as a downloader in malware families such as Carberp, Redyms and Gapz.

nodes.name: TDTESS
nodes.description: TDTESS is a 64-bit .NET binary backdoor used by CopyKittens.

nodes.name: Chinoxy
nodes.description: Chinoxy is a backdoor that has been used since at least November 2018, during the FunnyDream campaign, to gain persistence and drop additional payloads. According to security researchers, Chinoxy has been used by Chinese-speaking threat actors.

nodes.name: SharpStage
nodes.description: SharpStage is a .NET malware with backdoor capabilities.

nodes.name: PAKLOG
nodes.description: PAKLOG is a keylogger known to be leveraged by Mustang Panda and was first observed utilized in 2024. PAKLOG is deployed via a RAR archive (e.g., key.rar), which contains two files: a signed, legitimate binary (PACLOUD.exe) and the malicious PAKLOG DLL (pa_lang2.dll). The PACLOUD.exe binary is used to side-load the PAKLOG DLL which starts with the keylogger functionality.

nodes.name: COATHANGER
nodes.description: COATHANGER is a remote access tool (RAT) targeting FortiGate networking appliances. First used in 2023 in targeted intrusions against military and government entities in the Netherlands along with other victims, COATHANGER was disclosed in early 2024, with a high confidence assessment linking this malware to a state-sponsored entity in the People's Republic of China. COATHANGER is delivered after gaining access to a FortiGate device, with in-the-wild observations linked to exploitation of CVE-2022-42475. The name COATHANGER is based on a unique string in the malware used to encrypt configuration files on disk: “She took his coat and hung it up”.

nodes.name: Sardonic
nodes.description: Sardonic is a backdoor written in C and C++ that is known to be used by FIN8, as early as August 2021 to target a financial institution in the United States. Sardonic has a plugin system that can load specially made DLLs and execute their functions.

nodes.name: Smoke Loader
nodes.description: Smoke Loader is a malicious bot application that can be used to load other malware. Smoke Loader has been seen in the wild since at least 2011 and has included a number of different payloads. It is notorious for its use of deception and self-protection. It also comes with several plug-ins.

nodes.name: HALFBAKED
nodes.description: HALFBAKED is a malware family consisting of multiple components intended to establish persistence in victim networks.

nodes.name: WindTail
nodes.description: WindTail is a macOS surveillance implant used by Windshift. WindTail shares code similarities with Hack Back aka KitM OSX.

nodes.name: Misdat
nodes.description: Misdat is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm from 2010 to 2011.

nodes.name: reGeorg
nodes.description: reGeorg is an open-source web shell written in Python that can be used as a proxy to bypass firewall rules and tunnel data in and out of targeted networks.

nodes.name: FLIPSIDE
nodes.description: FLIPSIDE is a simple tool similar to Plink that is used by FIN5 to maintain access to victims.

nodes.name: Linux Rabbit
nodes.description: Linux Rabbit is malware that targeted Linux servers and IoT devices in a campaign lasting from August to October 2018. It shares code with another strain of malware known as Rabbot. The goal of the campaign was to install cryptocurrency miners onto the targeted servers and devices.

nodes.name: adbupd
nodes.description: adbupd is a backdoor used by PLATINUM that is similar to Dipsind.

nodes.name: Emissary
nodes.description: Emissary is a Trojan that has been used by Lotus Blossom. It shares code with Elise, with both Trojans being part of a malware group referred to as LStudio.

nodes.name: Exaramel for Linux
nodes.description: Exaramel for Linux is a backdoor written in the Go Programming Language and compiled as a 64-bit ELF binary. The Windows version is tracked separately under Exaramel for Windows.

nodes.name: KEYMARBLE
nodes.description: KEYMARBLE is a Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government.

nodes.name: BUBBLEWRAP
nodes.description: BUBBLEWRAP is a full-featured, second-stage backdoor used by the admin@338 group. It is set to run when the system boots and includes functionality to check, upload, and register plug-ins that can further enhance its capabilities.

nodes.name: HAWKBALL
nodes.description: HAWKBALL is a backdoor that was observed in targeting of the government sector in Central Asia.

nodes.name: TAMECAT
nodes.description: TAMECAT is a malware that is used by APT42 to execute PowerShell or C# content.

nodes.name: PS1
nodes.description: PS1 is a loader that was used to deploy 64-bit backdoors in the CostaRicto campaign.

nodes.name: HeartCrypt
nodes.description: HeartCrypt is a packer-as-a-service (PaaS) used to protect malware that has been available since at least 2024. HeartCrypt has been used to pack a variety of malware including Lumma Stealer, Remcos, and Rhadamanthys. In the HeartCrypt PaaS model, customers submit malware via private messaging services and it is then packed and returned by the operator as a new binary.

nodes.name: Ursnif
nodes.description: Ursnif is a banking trojan and variant of the Gozi malware observed being spread through various automated exploit kits, Spearphishing Attachments, and malicious links. Ursnif is associated primarily with data theft, but variants also include components (backdoors, spyware, file injectors, etc.) capable of a wide variety of behaviors.

nodes.name: CASTLETAP
nodes.description: CASTLETAP is an ICMP port knocking backdoor that has been installed on compromised FortiGate firewalls by UNC3886.

nodes.name: ThreatNeedle
nodes.description: ThreatNeedle is a backdoor that has been used by Lazarus Group since at least 2019 to target cryptocurrency, defense, and mobile gaming organizations. It is considered to be an advanced cluster of Lazarus Group's Manuscrypt (a.k.a. NukeSped) malware family.

nodes.name: RansomHub
nodes.description: RansomHub is a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) offering with Windows, ESXi, Linux, and FreeBSD versions that has been in use since at least 2024 to target organizations in multiple sectors globally. RansomHub operators may have purchased and rebranded resources from Knight (formerly Cyclops) Ransomware which shares infrastructure, feature, and code overlaps with RansomHub.

nodes.name: ZLib
nodes.description: ZLib is a full-featured backdoor that was used as a second-stage implant during Operation Dust Storm since at least 2014. ZLib is malware and should not be confused with the legitimate compression library from which its name is derived.

nodes.name: RedLeaves
nodes.description: RedLeaves is a malware family used by menuPass. The code overlaps with PlugX and may be based upon the open source tool Trochilus.

nodes.name: Miner-C
nodes.description: Miner-C is malware that mines victims for the Monero cryptocurrency. It has targeted FTP servers and Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices to spread.

nodes.name: POWERSOURCE
nodes.description: POWERSOURCE is a PowerShell backdoor that is a heavily obfuscated and modified version of the publicly available tool DNS_TXT_Pwnage. It was observed in February 2017 in spearphishing campaigns against personnel involved with United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings at various organizations. The malware was delivered when macros were enabled by the victim and a VBS script was dropped.

nodes.name: Tsundere Botnet
nodes.description: Tsundere Botnet is a botnet first reported in mid-2025 that is delivered via MSI installer or a PowerShell script. It leverages Node.js and JavaScript for payload delivery and execution, and uses smart contracts on the blockchain to host command and control (C2) addresses. Tsundere Botnet is attributed to a likely Russian-speaking threat actor.

nodes.name: LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA
nodes.description: LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA is a backdoor that was used by UNC5325 during Cutting Edge to deploy malware on targeted Ivanti Connect Secure VPNs and to establish persistence across system upgrades and patches.

nodes.name: Felismus
nodes.description: Felismus is a modular backdoor that has been used by Sowbug.

nodes.name: Zeus Panda
nodes.description: Zeus Panda is a Trojan designed to steal banking information and other sensitive credentials for exfiltration. Zeus Panda’s original source code was leaked in 2011, allowing threat actors to use its source code as a basis for new malware variants. It is mainly used to target Windows operating systems ranging from Windows XP through Windows 10.

nodes.name: GeminiDuke
nodes.description: GeminiDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2009 to 2012.

nodes.name: Havoc
nodes.description: Havoc is an open-source post-exploitation command and control (C2) framework first released on GitHub in October 2022 by C5pider (Paul Ungur), who continues to maintain and develop it with community contributors. Havoc provides a wide range of offensive security capabilities and has been adopted by multiple threat actors to establish and maintain control over compromised systems.

nodes.name: CARROTBAT
nodes.description: CARROTBAT is a customized dropper that has been in use since at least 2017. CARROTBAT has been used to install SYSCON and has infrastructure overlap with KONNI.

nodes.name: Matryoshka
nodes.description: Matryoshka is a malware framework used by CopyKittens that consists of a dropper, loader, and RAT. It has multiple versions; v1 was seen in the wild from July 2016 until January 2017. v2 has fewer commands and other minor differences.

nodes.name: FrameworkPOS
nodes.description: FrameworkPOS is a point of sale (POS) malware used by FIN6 to steal payment card data from sytems that run physical POS devices.

nodes.name: GravityRAT
nodes.description: GravityRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) and has been in ongoing development since 2016. The actor behind the tool remains unknown, but two usernames have been recovered that link to the author, which are "TheMartian" and "The Invincible." According to the National Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) of India, the malware has been identified in attacks against organization and entities in India.

nodes.name: WEBC2
nodes.description: WEBC2 is a family of backdoor malware used by APT1 as early as July 2006. WEBC2 backdoors are designed to retrieve a webpage, with commands hidden in HTML comments or special tags, from a predetermined C2 server.

nodes.name: Prestige
nodes.description: Prestige ransomware has been used by Sandworm Team since at least March 2022, including against transportation and related logistics industries in Ukraine and Poland in October 2022.

nodes.name: InvisibleFerret
nodes.description: InvisibleFerret is a modular python malware that is leveraged for data exfiltration and remote access capabilities. InvisibleFerret consists of four modules: main, payload, browser, and AnyDesk. InvisibleFerret malware has been leveraged by North Korea-affiliated threat actors identified as DeceptiveDevelopment or Contagious Interview since 2023. InvisibleFerret has historically been introduced to the victim environment through the use of the BeaverTail malware.

nodes.name: Bankshot
nodes.description: Bankshot is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first reported by the Department of Homeland Security in December of 2017. In 2018, Lazarus Group used the Bankshot implant in attacks against the Turkish financial sector.

nodes.name: SharpDisco
nodes.description: SharpDisco is a dropper developed in C# that has been used by MoustachedBouncer since at least 2020 to load malicious plugins.

nodes.name: StrongPity
nodes.description: StrongPity is an information stealing malware used by PROMETHIUM.

nodes.name: HAPPYWORK
nodes.description: HAPPYWORK is a downloader used by APT37 to target South Korean government and financial victims in November 2016.

nodes.name: xCaon
nodes.description: xCaon is an HTTP variant of the BoxCaon malware family that has used by IndigoZebra since at least 2014. xCaon has been used to target political entities in Central Asia, including Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

nodes.name: PLAINTEE
nodes.description: PLAINTEE is a malware sample that has been used by Rancor in targeted attacks in Singapore and Cambodia.

nodes.name: Pony
nodes.description: Pony is a credential stealing malware, though has also been used among adversaries for its downloader capabilities. The source code for Pony Loader 1.0 and 2.0 were leaked online, leading to their use by various threat actors.

nodes.name: WinMM
nodes.description: WinMM is a full-featured, simple backdoor used by Naikon.

nodes.name: Nebulae
nodes.description: Nebulae Is a backdoor that has been used by Naikon since at least 2020.

nodes.name: Janicab
nodes.description: Janicab is an OS X trojan that relied on a valid developer ID and oblivious users to install it.

nodes.name: AuditCred
nodes.description: AuditCred is a malicious DLL that has been used by Lazarus Group during their 2018 attacks.

nodes.name: ROAMINGHOUSE
nodes.description: ROAMINGHOUSE is a dropper malware used by MirrorFace to extract and execute embedded payloads including UPPERCUT components.

nodes.name: Lurid
nodes.description: Lurid is a malware family that has been used by several groups, including PittyTiger, in targeted attacks as far back as 2006.

nodes.name: TONESHELL
nodes.description: TONESHELL is a custom backdoor that has been used since at least Q1 2021. TONESHELL malware has previously been leveraged by Chinese affiliated actors identified as Mustang Panda.

nodes.name: UPSTYLE
nodes.description: UPSTYLE is a Python-based backdoor associated with exploitation of Palo Alto firewalls using CVE-2024-3400 in early 2024. UPSTYLE has only been observed in relation to this exploitation activity, which involved attempted install on compromised devices by the threat actor UTA0218.

nodes.name: Kasidet
nodes.description: Kasidet is a backdoor that has been dropped by using malicious VBA macros.

nodes.name: Hannotog
nodes.description: Hannotog is a type of backdoor malware uniquely assoicated with Lotus Blossom operations since at least 2022.

nodes.name: OceanSalt
nodes.description: OceanSalt is a Trojan that was used in a campaign targeting victims in South Korea, United States, and Canada. OceanSalt shares code similarity with SpyNote RAT, which has been linked to APT1.

nodes.name: Playcrypt
nodes.description: Playcrypt is a ransomware that has been used by Play since at least 2022 in attacks against against the business, government, critical infrastructure, healthcare, and media sectors in North America, South America, and Europe. Playcrypt derives its name from adding the .play extension to encrypted files and has overlap with tactics and tools associated with Hive and Nokoyawa ransomware and infrastructure associated with Quantum ransomware.

nodes.name: Brave Prince
nodes.description: Brave Prince is a Korean-language implant that was first observed in the wild in December 2017. It contains similar code and behavior to Gold Dragon, and was seen along with Gold Dragon and RunningRAT in operations surrounding the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.

nodes.name: Medusa Ransomware
nodes.description: Medusa Ransomware has been utilized in attacks since at least 2021. Medusa Ransomware has been known to be utilized in conjunction with living off the land techniques and remote management software.
